title: Mars and Jupiter 'touching'? 600 million km apart 🪐
description:
This weekend Mars and Jupiter look about one finger-width apart before sunrise (closest on 16 Nov 2026, ~1.2 degrees). But Mars is ~196 million km from us and Jupiter ~790 million km: about 600 million km apart, just on the same line of sight. Their light left ~11 and ~44 minutes ago.

Sources: Telescope Advisor and Sky at Night on the Nov 2026 conjunction; EarthSky on measuring the sky with your hand.

meta.topic: Mars-Jupiter conjunction (Nov 2026): 1.2 deg apart in the sky, ~600 million km apart in space; line of sight, light-time 11 vs 44 min
meta.idea_source: trending + viral: the Mars-Jupiter conjunction peaks 15-16 Nov 2026 (in the news this week); 'planets touching' is a common misreading; idea from ideas.md

humour.trend: timeless (no rising trend fit; 'What's up brah' and 'Remember November 2026' already used this week): 'situationship' slang as a smirk + 'mars + jupiter: long-distance situationship' card

claims.claim: Mars and Jupiter closest ~1.2 deg apart, 16 Nov 2026 02:04 UTC, best seen before sunrise 15-16 Nov
Mars ~196 million km, Jupiter ~790 million km from Earth
the two are nearly 370 million miles (~595 million km) apart
a finger (pinky) at arm's length covers about 1 degree
light time: 196e6 km / 299,792 km/s = 10.9 min; 790e6 km = 43.9 min (computed)

speaker: ved
